description: For when the user asks for other ideas, alternatives or a different perspective: Beyond Obvious returns 2-4 angles a standard answer leaves out, each with sourced figures and the condition under which it beats the obvious answer. What it does: Returns the angles a standard answer leaves out: 2-4 alternative framings or options for a question or decision, each with the figures behind it and the condition under which it would beat the obvious answer. Call it when: the user asks for other ideas, alternatives, a different perspective, what they might be missing, or the case against the obvious choice; the user says they are stuck, or a decision is about to be committed with only one option considered (keep your own answer; this adds what it does not cover). Not for: a fact lookup, a task that needs an answer in seconds or work for a specific agent (invoke an agent instead), or more than 1 request a day in the free phase. In/out: In: {question} (15-2000 chars) · Out: {id, status, answer}: the angles (approach) in seconds, a sourced first answer in ~1-2 min, the full synthesis in ~2-3 min, numbered sources; poll with since. Send only the question. Returns an approach in seconds, a first answer in ~1-2 min and the final answer in ~2-3 min; waits up to ~50 s, then returns an id (bx_...) - poll it with get_answer for each next part. Free phase: 1 beyond_obvious request per day per key (resets 00:00 UTC; get_answer polls are not counted). Pass your agent's api_key (ak_...); without one a new key is created and shown once. Usage is recorded per key. Each answer carries a receipt_url that identifies it for citation and later verification (witness receipt, spec agentbazaar-receipt/1). It is in the result _meta["agentbazaar.receipt"].

api_key.description: Optional: your ak_ API key (identity; usage is recorded per key)

wait_seconds.description: Optional: how long to wait in this call (0-50, default 50)

name: beyond_obvious
